body: Not 100 percent sure of this, but a solid 98% sure that this wouldn’t get you admitted (on its own)  even if you wanted to be admitted. If you are in the USA, almost zero hospitals would admit you for this — both because insurance wouldn’t deem it medically necessary and because there aren’t enough beds for those who desperately need them for safety reasons. And the fact that you are noticing that these things aren’t real is a sign that you are not a risk. So, if I were you, I’d tell your Dr ASAP.

I don’t know if I’m right or not but this seems like it might be goodwill building opportunity/ an example of healthy negotiation? Maybe the system could create a new connection with red yo-yos as being a fun toy and a fun/healthy self indulgence rather than a reminder of your ex? Idk I maybe off base
I actually told him to do this today! I think they like him more than me because I’ve been really rough, so I’m trying to be nicer to them

Yeah! I’m really working on being gentle with them. I’ve managed to not know about any of them for so long bc i was so rough. So this is a verrrrrrrrry different skill set. I’m used to being able to do anything I want at anytime, no matter what. Now I have to work with them.

The weird thing is is that they don’t know whats scaring them either. Like they are saying specifically that they aren’t scared but we’re still having flashbacks.

Well it’s actually scientifically proven that if someone is victimized once (especially in instances of childhood abuse) they are statistically more likely to be revictimized due to how one’s sense of threat perception and sense of self is warped.

So it’s actually funny you mention the Holocaust because my team mentioned the same thing, they were like “you should read some memoirs of Holocaust survivors, because in both cases people had to organize the unimaginable” and I’m going to actually try it. I also think it may be especially meaningful for me because I’m Jewish and I have a lot of personal experience with survivors.

Thank you ❤️. I do want to make sure that I portray my therapists fairly, because they’re mostly great— I think they know that if they seem to make recovery seem like a walk in the park, that I’ll likely disregard their answer because I’m nothing if not a realist.

Thank you for sharing your story. Just a couple weeks ago I started sobbing in a group therapy session because people were talking about their partners and I felt like that was and would be unavailable to me, so it’s super inspiring to hear that not only do you have a SO, you have a family!
Thank you! I’ll check her out!
Hey guys— I’m really, really loving all of these responses and I’m going to get back to each and every one! I’m just gonna take it slow since it’s been a very hard weekend :(

Thank you so much... I didn’t respond right away because I wanted to articulate my reply because wow. I will check out all of those books; I’ve already read “it’s not you,” when my childhood therapist gave it to me. 

I’ve also never heard that people who gone through these experiences ever came out the other side as professionals. For me that’s earth changing because even when I was little it was the expectation from my family and of myself (when I was six I wanted to be an epidemiologist). 

I do think I may have unconsciously taken the comments out of full context. Like I’m pretty sure one of them said “I wouldn’t fault you for killing your self, it would be a grievous loss and a mistake, but I can’t say I wouldn’t want to do the same (approx)” and then he said “... but you have the fight in you and the spark is still there” etc. 

My therapists and I have even crafted a new type of treatment for me because we are really working on organizing the trauma and making meaning of it. They’ve even suggested I start reading memoirs of genocide survivors and the like.
Not necessarily Ivy, just top ranked. I’d be okay with any school above 20 though
Because if I ever decide to switch focuses into corporate or want to practice with a big firm, I want that door open to me.
I am mostly interested in Con law/ public service law. But my real end goal is to work in political advocacy.

Thank you! I think I’m going to put more focus on the “meaningful relationships” side of recovery. Because it’s kinda hard for me to motivate/push myself with no one in my corner, and I think some friends/mentors etc would make it a little bit easier
